The query field cannot be changed after object creation
Identical, already-correct configuration is redone unnecessarily on every call
SearchAPI objects cannot be cloned at all

questions.title: Drawbacks of Manual Object Copying
questions.question: (Theory) Why is it usually a bad idea for client code to copy an object by manually setting each field from outside the class (e.g., copy.os = original.os, copy.runtime = original.runtime, ...)?

options.optionText: It runs slower than every other approach in all cases
It creates tight coupling to internal fields, can violate encapsulation, and leads to isinstance() chains for subclasses
Python does not allow assigning attributes from outside a class
It only works for classes with exactly two fields

questions.title: Mutating Registry Templates Directly
questions.question:
(Scenario) A registry is being used like this:

```python
registry = VMImageRegistry()
registry.register("backend-server-v3", backend_image)

server = registry.get("backend-server-v3")
server.hostname = "web-01"
```

Note: .clone() was never called before modifying server. What is the risk here?

options.optionText: None — get() already returns a safe, independent copy
This code will raise an error because hostname doesn't exist yet
server is the same object stored inside the registry, so this directly modifies the shared template itself
The registry will automatically detect and block this change

questions.title: Shallow Copy Using copy Module
questions.question:
(Code Output)

```python
import copy

class Config:
    def __init__(self):
        self.settings = {"debug": True}

original = Config()
shallow = copy.copy(original)
shallow.settings["debug"] = False

print(original.settings["debug"])
```

What gets printed?

options.optionText: True
None
An error is raised
False

questions.title: When to Skip Prototype
questions.question: (Theory) According to the lecture, when is it reasonable to skip the Prototype pattern entirely and just construct an object normally?

options.optionText: When constructing the object fresh is already cheap and simple, so cloning would just add unnecessary overhead
Never — Prototype must always be used, even for the simplest classes
Only when the class has no fields at all
Only when the class is abstract

questions.title: Separating Prototype and Registry Concerns
questions.question: (Scenario) A registry needs to store several different “welcome email”, “password reset email”, and “invoice email” templates, and retrieve/clone the right one by name whenever a new email needs to be sent. Which two responsibilities does this design split apart, according to the lecture?

options.optionText: Validation and testing
Copying an object (Prototype) and storing/retrieving templates by key (Registry)
Sending the email and formatting the email
Creating the class and deleting the class

questions.title: Core Problem Solved by Prototype Pattern
questions.question: (Theory) What problem does the Prototype pattern mainly solve?

options.optionText: Creating a new object by copying an existing one instead of building it from scratch
Creating an object step-by-step with validation before it is complete
Making sure only one object of a class ever exists
Choosing which subclass to create based on user input

questions.title: Thread Safety in Prototype Registry
questions.question:
(Code Debug) A student writes this registry method to add a new prototype only if it doesn't already exist:

```python
def add_if_missing(self, key, prototype):
    if key not in self._templates:
        self._templates[key] = prototype
```

Why might this method behave incorrectly if two threads call it at the same time with the same new key?

options.optionText: Python dictionaries cannot store custom objects as values
abstractmethod prevents this method from ever running twice
The check ("is key missing?") and the action ("add it") are two separate steps, so both threads can pass the check before either one writes
Python automatically locks every dictionary method, so this is actually safe

questions.title: Multiple Constructors in Python
questions.question: (Scenario) A Student class has an __init__ that takes no arguments and sets default values. A developer wants to also let Student be created by copying an existing Student object. They try adding a second __init__ method that takes a source object instead. What actually happens in Python?

options.optionText: Python raises an error because a class cannot have two constructors
Both __init__ methods work — Python picks the right one based on the arguments passed
Python merges both __init__ methods into one automatically
Only the second __init__ definition remains active; the first one is silently overwritten

questions.title: Overriding Clone in Subclasses
questions.question: (Theory) Why must every subclass of a Prototype-based class override clone() itself, even if the parent class already has a clone() method?

options.optionText: Because if it doesn’t, calling .clone() runs the parent’s version, which doesn’t know about the subclass’s extra fields — silently dropping them
Because Python requires every subclass to redefine every inherited method
Because clone() is not inherited in Python
Because subclasses are not allowed to call super().__init__()

options.optionText: Python raises a KeyError immediately, right on this line

questions.title: Prototype vs. Registry Pattern
questions.question: (Theory) Which statement best describes the difference between the Prototype pattern and the Registry pattern?

options.optionText: Prototype lets an object copy itself; Registry stores and retrieves reusable templates by key
Prototype stores multiple templates by name; Registry copies a single object
They are the same pattern with two different names
Prototype is only used in Python; Registry is only used in Java
